items.item_text: 01. All applicants are required to submit responses to the following supplemental questions. Your responses will provide information about your background and experience related to this position and will be used in the screening and selection process. Be concise yet specific and informative in your responses to these supplemental questions. "See resume," attachments or links will not be accepted as a substitute for your responses to the questions in the following boxes. Incomplete responses will not be considered. Please indicate below that you have read and understand these instructions. Options: Yes | No
02. I have completed all sections of the application including references. (Statements such as "see resume" will not be acceptable.) Options: Yes | No
03. Please specify your highest level of education. Options: High School or equivalent (GED) | Associate's Degree | Bachelor's Degree | Master's Degree | Juris Doctor | Doctorate Degree
04. Please indicate the field in which you have earned your degree in:

05. How many years of professional experience do you have managing information technology projects? Options: No experience | Less than 1 year | 1 year to less than 2 years | 2 years to less than 3 years | 3 years to less than 5 years | 5 or more years

06. Indicate where you have worked to obtain experience in managing information technology projects. What was the time frame, what was the employer's name and describe the work performed. (You must complete this section).
07. Describe a time when you were responsible for multiple IT projects with competing deadlines and limited resources. How did you determine priorities and ensure critical milestones were met?

08. Which statement best describes your level of responsibility for IT projects? Options: I have participated as a member of a project team. | I have coordinated specific portions or phases of IT projects. | I have independently managed IT projects from planning through completion. | I have managed multiple concurrent IT projects or a portfolio of projects. | I do not have professional IT project management experience.

09. Please indicate any current professional certifications you possess. Options: Project Management Professional (PMP) | Registered Communications Distribution Designer (RCDD) | Other BICSI certification | Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) | Agile/Scrum certification | Other project management or IT infrastructure certification | None of the above
10. If you selected “Other,” please identify the certification(s).

11. Provide an example of an IT or infrastructure project in which you were responsible for monitoring the budget, schedule, procurement, and/or project risks. What challenges arose, what actions did you take, and what was the outcome?

12. Please indicate the areas in which you have professional project management experience. Select all that apply. Options: Low-voltage IT infrastructure | Structured cabling | Network infrastructure/network rooms | Wireless/networking systems | Audiovisual (AV) systems | IP-based physical security systems | New building construction | Building modernization or renovation | Bond-funded capital projects | Deferred maintenance projects | IT equipment procurement | Public works projects | None of the above

13. Which best describes your experience coordinating IT infrastructure with building construction or modernization projects? Options: No experience | Limited involvement as a project team member | Responsible for coordinating specific IT components | Managed IT infrastructure throughout multiple phases of construction | Served as the primary IT project manager/representative throughout the construction lifecycle

14. Describe how you have demonstrated sensitivity and understanding in delivery of services and support to a diverse workforce and student population (diverse in terms of socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic background). This section is required.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
Registered Communications Distribution Designer (RCDD) or similar Building Industry Consulting Service International (BICSI) certification.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Management Information Systems, or a related field.
Associate degree in Business, Management Information Systems, or a related field.
Five (5) years of experience in information technology. Two (2) years of IT project management.
Three (3) years of experience working on large-scale new construction or bond-funded projects.
Seven (7) years of experience in information technology. Two (2) years of IT project management.
Experience with California Public Works procurement and bidding processes.
Expertise in developing, monitoring, and managing project budgets, and experience in cost estimation, financial reporting, and identifying potential financial risks.
Analyzes, directs, and manages the installation, construction, upgrade, replacement and/or deferred maintenance of various low-voltage IT and networking systems district-wide.
Coordinates IT project activities with Facilities Services, architects, and MEP engineers to ensure technology requirements are integrated into physical building designs.
Serves as the primary IT liaison during planning and construction; reviews architectural blueprints to identify and mitigate technology omissions before construction begins.
Plans technology projects to ensure goals are met on schedule; prioritizes long-lead time equipment procurement (e.g., switches, UPS) to align with building completion dates.
Monitors project technology budgets; identifies and evaluates risks; ensures bond-fund eligibility for all technology expenses and escalates issues to management.
Reviews proposals, conducts feasibility analysis, and establishes communication plans; coordinates with the IT Project Manager on District-wide technology standards.
Ensures project compliance with Division of the State Architect (DSA) requirements, California Public Contract Code, and bond funding mandates.
Conducts walkthroughs and audits; ensures a satisfactory transition of "care, custody, and control" of IT products (e.g., AV systems, Smart Classrooms) to the end-users upon building completion.
Maintains project documentation in collaboration with project sponsors, involved stakeholders, and the IT Project Manager.

Participates in project management meetings during preliminary planning, bidding, and construction phases, representing the technology interests of the District by interfacing with architects, engineers, or contractors as required by the various projects.
Participates in the development and continuous improvement of the District's project proposals, charters, plans, reviews, and prioritization processes.
Participates in the developing, prioritizing, budgeting, and planning of projects, project portfolio management and related initiatives.
Performs other duties as assigned.
Two (2) years of IT project management.
In-depth understanding of low-voltage IT, networking systems, IP-based physical security, and complex AV integration.
Two (2) years of IT project management.

Understanding of the principles of quality assurance and quality control across both construction and technology infrastructure projects (e.g., structured cabling, network rooms, low-voltage systems, hardware deployment, and facility modernization).
Familiarity with Agile, Waterfall, and construction management best practices using tools such as Asana.
Understanding of construction processes, facilities management, and how IT infrastructure projects integrate with ongoing and future construction projects.
Expertise in managing multi-million dollar technology budgets, including cost estimation and bond-fund reporting.
Proficiency in identifying potential risks, evaluating their impact on projects, and developing strategies to mitigate or eliminate these risks.
Capable of reviewing project proposals, conducting feasibility studies, and providing well-informed recommendations based on analysis and alignment with organizational goals.
This is primarily a sedentary office classification although standing and walking between work areas may be required.
Positions in this classification may occasionally bend, stoop, kneel, reach, push, and pull drawers open and closed to retrieve and file information.
Employees work in an office environment with moderate noise levels and controlled temperature conditions.
Employees may interact with upset staff and/or public and private representatives in interpreting and enforcing departmental policies and procedures.
Project Management
Budget and Resource Management
Stakeholder Management
Regulatory Compliance
Problem-Solving and Decision-Making

Ability to effectively coordinate with various stakeholders, including Facilities Services, administrators, equipment suppliers, and contractors, to ensure alignment and timely progression of projects.

Strong verbal and written communication skills to effectively liaise with project teams, stakeholders, and management, including the ability to present complex technical information in an understandable manner.
Ability to ensure that projects comply with all relevant regulations, funding requirements, and contractual obligations, and maintain high standards of quality throughout the project lifecycle.

Proficient in maintaining comprehensive project documentation and ensuring a smooth transition of IT products and systems at project completion, including effective handover to relevant stakeholders or departments.

Must possess mobility to work in a standard office setting and use standard office equipment, including a computer; vision to read printed materials and a computer screen; and hearing and speech to communicate in person, before groups, and over the telephone.
Finger dexterity is needed to access, enter, and retrieve data using a computer keyboard, typewriter keyboard, or calculator and to operate standard office equipment.
Employees must possess the ability to lift, carry, push, and pull materials and objects up to 25 pounds.
Technical Knowledge
Communication Skills
Organizational and Time Management Skills
